summary: Iteration 13 — Duplicate detection in POST /api/capture (backend + frontend routes). Backend: added /app/backend/tests/test_iteration13_duplicates.py — 6/6 PASSED (15.9s). Verified: (a) /capture response always includes `duplicates` list; (b) after seeding a TEST_ item that matches the AI-derived analysis (same category + colour/style/fabric/pattern), a subsequent /capture surfaces it as a duplicate with the required shape {id, name, category, colour, photo}; (c) items in a DIFFERENT category are never returned — all returned duplicates strictly match the analysis category. Regressions confirmed: /capture still returns {analysis, clean_image, duplicates}; POST /api/items still accepts the bulk-add body and coerces price='' → null (via the new field_validator on ItemCreate). Frontend: /add-item and /bulk-add both load in the web preview without red screen or unmatched route. testIDs verified: add-item-close, add-item-bulk, add-photo-hanging (initial state has no `add-item-duplicates` banner as expected — banner only renders after analysis returns dupes); bulk-back is present. Native photo picker cannot open in web preview (Playwright confirms 'File chooser dialog can only be shown with a user activation.') — the actual dup banner + dup-<id> tap → /item/[id] navigation could not be exercised end-to-end from web, but the JSX wiring is verified by code review (add-item.tsx L219-242 uses testIDs add-item-duplicates, dup-dismiss, dup-<id> and router.replace to /item/[id]; bulk-add.tsx L52 flags rows with dupe badge and 'Possible dupe' label; done-summary L110 references dupes count).
action_items: None from this iteration — duplicate detection contract is honoured end-to-end and both frontend routes load cleanly. Nice-to-have for future iterations: (1) surface the SCORE alongside each duplicate so the UI could sort/label 'strong match' vs 'possible match' when the threshold is lowered; (2) consider expanding find_similar_items to also weight name/brand for even higher precision; (3) once user completes a real capture flow (native device or Expo Go), verify visually that dup-<id> tap navigates to the item detail screen — cannot be automated in web preview.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py find_similar_items (L797-831) is O(N) over the full wardrobe on every /capture. Fine for typical wardrobes (<1k items) but if a user has 10k+ pieces (unlikely) this in-memory scoring will start to matter. Not urgent.

server.py L857 fetches up to 1000 items (`to_list(1000)`); large wardrobes past 1000 items would silently miss duplicates. Consider using a Mongo aggregation with $match on category for O(matches) instead of O(wardrobe).

server.py L858 — find_similar_items relies on the AI-returned `style/fabric/pattern` strings being canonicalised; a mismatch of 'Cotton' vs 'cotton knit' will drop the score. Both sides are lowercased via _norm() but not stemmed. Acceptable for MVP but low-recall for anything phrased slightly differently.

add-item.tsx L231 uses router.replace to navigate to /item/[id] on tapping a duplicate — replace() means the new-piece form state is destroyed and back button jumps past it. router.push may be more forgiving (user can tap 'X, add anyway' after peeking).

bulk-add.tsx L136 shows 'Possible dupe' as the ONLY label for flagged rows, hiding the AI-inferred name. If a user is scanning the grid they lose the piece identity; consider showing name plus a small badge instead of replacing name.

success_rate.frontend: route load + testID wiring verified; end-to-end dup banner not exercisable in web preview (native picker)
